items.q: Painful submandibular swelling surging at mealtimes and easing after most likely is what?
items.exp: Stone obstructing Wharton duct backs saliva at secretory demand causing mealtime gland swelling; floor of mouth palpation and ultrasound find most stones. Tumours persist independent of meals.
r: Incorrect. Tumour mass is constant.
Correct. Mealtime submandibular stone colic.
Incorrect. Ludwig is woody bilateral emergency.
Incorrect. Branchial cyst sits sternomastoid edge.

items.q: Why does submandibular gland form most salivary stones?
o: Alkaline mucin rich saliva flowing uphill against gravity in long duct
items.exp: Wharton duct length, upward course, viscous calcium rich secretion predispose precipitation, unlike serous parotid flow downhill. Hence about four fifths of stones submandibular.
r: Incorrect. Size not cause.
Correct. Uphill mucinous calcium flow stones.
Incorrect. Long duct is itself factor.
Incorrect. Viruses cause parotitis, not stones.

items.q: Commonest benign parotid tumour and its correct surgical principle is what?
o: Pleomorphic adenoma; superficial parotidectomy with facial nerve preservation, not enucleation
items.exp: Pleomorphic adenoma pseudopods breach capsule, so enucleation seeds recurrence (and multinodular relapse endangers nerve later); formal superficial parotidectomy with nerve dissection is standard for superficial lobe tumours.
r: Incorrect. Warthin is second and selected observation debated.
Correct. Pleomorphic adenoma, nerve sparing parotidectomy.
Incorrect. Lipoma not commonest salivary tumour.
Incorrect. Haemangioma is infant lesion different pathway.

items.q: Sweating and flushing over cheek while eating months after parotidectomy is which syndrome and mechanism?
o: Frey syndrome: parasympathetic fibres regrow to sweat glands
items.exp: Auriculotemporal parasympathetics meant for parotid misdirect to cutaneous sweat glands and vessels (aberrant regeneration), so gustatory stimulus sweats skin; starch iodine test maps it, botulinum treats severe cases.
r: Incorrect. Horner is sympathetic eye signs.
Correct. Frey gustatory sweating.
Incorrect. First bite is pain with first mouthful after deep lobe or sympathetic injury.
Incorrect. Sjogren dries glands systemically.
items.kp: Eats and cheek sweats: Frey rewiring.

items.q: Rule of thumb for salivary tumour malignancy probability by gland size is what?
o: Smaller the gland, greater proportion malignant (sublingual and minor highest)
items.exp: Rough proportions invert with size: parotid about 20 percent malignant, submandibular near half, minor and sublingual majority malignant, so small gland masses biopsy urgently.
r: Incorrect. Parotid mostly benign.
Correct. Small gland, sinister odds.
Incorrect. Proportions differ markedly.
Incorrect. Submandibular cancers common.
items.kp: Tiny gland lump, big cancer chance.

items.q: Commonest malignant salivary tumour overall, graded from low cystic to high solid, is what?
items.exp: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma leads malignant salivary tumours (parotid especially), prognosis by grade; adenoid cystic is notorious perineural but second in frequency teaching.
r: Incorrect. Adenoid cystic second classic.
Correct. Mucoepidermoid commonest malignant.
Incorrect. Acinic less common.
Incorrect. Primary squamous is uncommon diagnosis of exclusion.

items.q: Adenoid cystic carcinoma signature behaviour causing pain and very late recurrences is what?
o: Perineural invasion and indolent late lung metastases over decades
items.exp: Tumour tracks nerves causing pain and paraesthesia, skips nodes relatively, and metastasises to lungs after many years despite local control, needing lifelong follow up and generous nerve margin planning.
r: Incorrect. Early blood spread not signature.
Correct. Perineural creep, decades late lungs.
Incorrect. Nodes relatively spared.
Incorrect. No secretory syndrome.
items.kp: Creeps nerves, returns in lungs at year fifteen.

items.q: Bilateral painful parotid swelling with fever in unvaccinated child plus orchitis in adolescent brother suggests what?
items.exp: Mumps classically swells both parotids (one may lead) with systemic features and extrasalivary orchitis, pancreatitis or meningitis; bacterial parotitis is unilateral pus in dehydrated elderly.
r: Incorrect. Bacterial is unilateral elderly pus.
Correct. Mumps bilateral viral pattern.
Incorrect. Sjogren chronic dry autoimmune adult.
Incorrect. Stones colic with meals unilateral.
items.kp: Both parotids plus orchitis equals mumps.

items.q: Persistent hard unilateral parotid enlargement developing in longstanding Sjogren patient raises concern for what?
items.exp: Chronic B cell stimulation in Sjogren multiplies lymphoma risk (MALT type in parotid), so new persistent, hard or rapidly enlarging gland, nodes or B symptoms need biopsy pathway.
r: Incorrect. Stones colic intermittently, not hard growth.
Correct. Lymphoma transformation vigilance.
Incorrect. Frey is post surgical sweating.
Incorrect. Warthin is smoker older male pattern separate.
items.kp: Sjogren gland turning hard: biopsy for lymphoma.

items.q: Second commonest benign parotid tumour in older male smokers, often bilateral at parotid tail, is what?
items.exp: Warthin tumour (papillary cystadenoma lymphomatosum) associates smoking, older men, parotid tail cystic masses and bilaterality about a tenth, with very low malignant change.
r: Incorrect. Pleomorphic is first commonest, solitary female tilt.
Correct. Warthin of older male smokers.
Incorrect. Oncocytoma rarer.
Incorrect. Basal adenoma less classic vignette.
items.kp: Smoking grandfather, tail cysts both sides: Warthin.
